title: Emergency handback dipstick sheet
body:
Purpose:
Quick cross-functional tracker to capture who can cover short handbacks (2–72 hours), approximate capacity, immediate blockers, and a tiny cost/back-of-envelope impact so ops/product can triage and commit. This is intentionally minimal — use when an endpoint surge or regional fallbacks require fast manual coverage decisions.

How to use (2-min):
1) Scan the list and mark a tentative owner (Y/N) — no formal handoff until Slack confirmation.
2) If owner = Y, estimate available capacity in hours and whether they can cover cold-start or hot-failover.
3) Flag any infra blockers (network, KMS, VPN) or policy blockers (customer data, region).
4) If >24h expected, move to formal handoff doc and assign an ops incident ticket.

Columns (sheet view):
- owner_name | role | contact | can_cover (Y/N) | window (hours) | est_hours_available | expected_latency_impact | blockers | notes/action items | escalations (if any)

Current snapshot (hand-entered):
- Lena Morales | Solutions Eng | lena@redwood.ai | Y | 8 | 6 | +40–80ms | needs vpn creds | Will take first 2hr triage then hand to James | Slack: #se-solutions
- James O'Neill | Platform Eng | james@redwood.ai | Y | 24 | 16 | +20–50ms | dependent on region-us-west quota | Can scale using dedicated pool if approved | JIRA: ENG-7432
- Priya Kumar | SRE | priya@redwood.ai | N | 0 | 0 | n/a | on leave til 11/26 | fallback to SRE-rotation
- Matteo Rossi | Infra | matteo@redwood.ai | Y | 4 | 3 | +100ms if cold spin | GPU pool cold-start | Matteo will pre-warm 1 node (manual)

Quick econ sentence:
- Rough unit cost for 12h handback coverage (warm path): ~12h * 0.25 FTE equiv = 3 FTE-hours. If using dedicated burst GPUs add ~ $45–120 depending on instance type. Use this to prioritize owner selection when multiple asks.

Open questions / edge cases (notes to self):
- If coverage crosses regions, who owns legal/data gating for cached prefixes? (Raised to legal via OPS-211)
- Can we temporarily route low-priority traffic to a compatible quantized variant to reduce cost? (Ask Applied ML: Matteo)
- For customer PII-sensitive routes, only product or SE may approve manual handback — add explicit approval checkbox next version.

Immediate actions (today):
- [ ] Confirm Lena can start triage at 09:00 PST (Asha)
- [ ] James to open quick capacity request for us-west dedicated pool (James)
- [ ] Matteo to attempt 1-node pre-warm and report cold-start time (Matteo)
- [ ] If coverage > 12h then escalate to incident commander and create OPS-incident ticket (Asha)

Mini postmortem capture fields (if event > 24h):
- time_started | time_ended | primary_owner | tickets | outcome_summary | lessons (1–3 bullets)

Short heuristics for picking owners:
- If <4 hours required -> choose on-call or nearest-available SE (low context cost).
- If >=4 and <24 -> platform or SE with capacity, prioritize those who can pre-warm.
- If >=24 -> formal handoff to SRE/ops with ticket and runbook.

Shortcuts / macros (column notes):
- "prewarm=Y" -> owner commits to pre-warm node(s) and set ticket for decommission.
- "data-check=required" -> route to product/legal for approval before any manual log access.

References / quick links (put back into sheet links):
- Fallback route playbook: confluence.redwood.ai/fallbacks
- Dedicated pool request template: GH: runtime/.github/dedicated-request-template.md
- Legal gating for cached tokens: OPS-211 (linked above)

Notes to self (loose):
- Keep this sheet minimal; don’t attempt to be an exhaustive runbook. The goal is speed.
- Next iteration: add an auto-refresh of owner availability from on-call roster (but that needs SSO-read access).

End.
